quote_text:
Yeah, it was hard-fought points.  Hard-fought points as well.
Difficult game because of the conditions  and the pitch, obviously. Actually felt it  
probably played better than I thought  it was going to, to be honest. Yeah,  
we’ve had to grind it out — fine margins,  as it’s been in all the games we’ve played  
against St Johnstone. But it’s an important  three points. After having lost last week,  
to bounce back and win — that sets  us up nicely for an important week.
Did you change your approach at all because  of the conditions when you turned up today?
Not our approach, no. You just speak about  certain moments in the game that might happen.  
The mentality in these games is really important  because, with the wind, the pitch, the rain — it’s  
not easy sometimes to judge the ball, the bounce  of the ball. Your touch or control can be off a  
little bit, and that can affect you. So it’s about  controlling the things we can control. You’ve  
got to show real perseverance in terms of your  mindset, and I felt we did that, to be honest.
How important were Elion and James with their  
movement? Why did you want them to  move wide to open up St Johnstone?
Yeah, when you’re playing against a back  three, sometimes the spaces are outside  
their back three with the wing-backs  high. But it always depends on where  
the three are on the pitch — every situation  is different. Sometimes it might be outside,  
sometimes they might stretch, and it  might allow you to dive back inside them.
For the second goal, we played  through them — through the middle  
of the pitch — and then Elion was on the  outside of the right-sided center-back,  
down the side. That’s what you’re trying to  do, but again, it’s not always easy to execute.
It seemed like Michael took a lot  of joy in that pass into Shankland?
Yeah, no — that’s exactly it. When you play this  formation, you can overload the middle of the  
pitch if you’re prepared to make those passes  — which isn’t always easy, especially today.
Michael waits on the ball, he pauses,  which is really important because that  
allows the players to get into the  right positions. That extra one or  
two seconds gives Shanks time to get  into position to receive the pass.
Sometimes, that kind of patience can  make people anxious when defenders are  
on the ball for a bit of time, but not  with Michael or Jamie. They’re calm,  
they’re good on the ball. It was a terrific pass  through the middle of the pitch, and Shanks turns,  
slides a lovely weighted pass through,  and Elion finishes it off brilliantly.
Craig Gordon showed just how vital it is to have a  
good goalkeeper — that save before  the second goal was incredible.
Yeah, it was an incredible save. A match-winning  save. Doesn’t surprise me, though — you see it  
every day in training. The way he trains, the  way he conducts himself — he’s invaluable to us.
And then, we go down the other end — a minute  or two later — and score the winner. That’s  
the fine margins in this game. With anyone  else, it probably would’ve been a goal,  
but Craig’s reflexes and reactions  are unbelievable. Fantastic stop.
Elion Kangu really bounced back today —  how pleased were you with his response?
Yeah, massive. So pleased for Elion.  He’s such a positive guy — so infectious.  
Exactly the type of character  we want to bring to Hearts.
Yeah, he was disappointed after last week —  naturally — but he didn’t let it affect him.  
He bounced back today. And because of his  outstanding mentality, he gets the rewards.
His first goal — a great goal, a proper  center-forward’s goal. He’s right in  
there to tap it in. And then his second  goal — he just puts his foot through it,  
goes for it, and hammers  it home. Delighted for him.
The league position — you’re now a point  off the top six. Was that an important one,  
especially after most of the  teams above you won yesterday?
Yeah, but we can only control what we can control.
It was important for us to  bounce back from last week  
with a good performance and pick  up three points — and we did that.
It’s the start of a big week. Nine points on the  table — six now — and the league could look very  
different come the end of the game against Hibs  next Sunday. This was a really big three points.
Have you started looking at the league table?
No, I haven’t. I saw the results yesterday,  so I know that affected where we were.
But if you look at where we were,  compared to where we are now,  
and the points we’ve gained — we’re  improving. We’re in good form. I  
don’t know how many games it’s been, but  we’ve only lost one in quite a while now.
Near the end of the season — six games  left before the split — our aim is to  
finish in the top six. How many games  we’ll need to win to do that? Who knows.
On Cammy Devlin — he missed out today.  What’s the latest on him? And how important  
has Benny been stepping into that role?
Yeah, Cammy’s not quite right, unfortunately. He  trained this week, but we had to take a step back.  
He had some effects after the session, didn’t feel  right, so we had to let him rest and start again.
It’s been frustrating — for him and  for us — but his health is the most  
important thing. We’ll look after  him, and we won’t take any chances.
Benny’s been brilliant. Playing as  a single six isn’t easy — sometimes  
he’s on his own in there — but  he’s covered the ground really  
well. Thought he was excellent against  Rangers last week, and again today.
He does so much unnoticed work — the ugly side  of the game. Interceptions, regains, breaks up  
play — and then helps set up counter-attacks.  Last two games, he’s been fantastic.
Do you hope Cammy will be back for next week?
Yeah, we still hope so. It happened late Friday,  so there’s time. We’ll take it day by day,  
monitor him, and see how he is. We’re not ruling  him out, that’s for sure. But again — no chances.
And on formation — you played quite narrow  
today, but you weren’t really  exposed. How did you manage that?
Yeah, it’s a balance. You want to be compact  and play together when you’re defending.
With St Johnstone, you’re not always sure.  They’ve been quite consistent recently,  
but they do change shape during  games. Early in the season,  
they played with a diamond. More  recently, it’s been more of a box.
We wanted to match their numbers in  the middle of the pitch — take away  
their overload. They gave us  problems here earlier in the  
season — late October or November — so  we wanted to take away that advantage.
But by doing that, you lose a  bit of width higher up the pitch.
We also knew that with Elion, James, and Shanks  — all who play a bit differently — if we could  
win the ball and break, we’d get  into situations where we could go  
three-vs-three against their  backline. That’s what you want.
Didn’t always come off today  — sometimes one better pass or  
a better final ball and we’d have  had more joy. But that’s football.
title: Neil Critchley Post Match Interview | St Johnstone 1-2 Hearts
